practiceQuestions.q: Under which act was the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India established?
practiceQuestions.sol: The NHRC is a statutory body established in October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

practiceQuestions.q: What type of body is the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)?
practiceQuestions.sol: The NHRC is a statutory body because it was created by an Act of Parliament (Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993), not directly by the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: Who serves as the ex-officio chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities, who is also a member of the NHRC?
opts: Chairperson of the National Commission for SCs
Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities
Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
practiceQuestions.sol: The NHRC has several ex-officio members, including the chairpersons of the National Commission for Minorities, National Commission for SCs, National Commission for STs, and National Commission for Women, among others.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the tenure of the Chairperson and members of the National Human Rights Commission as amended by the 2019 amendment act?
opts: 5 years or until attaining the age of 70 years
3 years or until attaining the age of 70 years
5 years or until attaining the age of 65 years
6 years or until attaining the age of 65 years
practiceQuestions.sol: Originally, the tenure was 5 years or up to 70 years. The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 reduced the tenure to 3 years or until they attain 70 years of age, whichever is earlier, and made them eligible for re-appointment.

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following can be appointed as the Chairperson of the NHRC as per the 2019 amendment?
opts: Only a sitting judge of the Supreme Court
A retired Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court
Any eminent jurist appointed by the President
practiceQuestions.sol: Originally, only a retired Chief Justice of India could be NHRC Chairperson. The 2019 amendment expanded it to include a Judge of the Supreme Court as well.

practiceQuestions.q: Who appoints the Chairperson and members of the National Human Rights Commission?
opts: A committee comprising Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman
practiceQuestions.sol: The Chairperson and members are appointed by the President of India on the recommendations of a high-powered committee headed by the Prime Minister.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is NOT a member of the selection committee that recommends appointments to the NHRC?
opts: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: The selection committee consists of the Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Leaders of the Opposition in both Houses, and the Union Home Minister. The CJI is NOT a member of this selection committee.

practiceQuestions.q: Where is the headquarters of the National Human Rights Commission located?
practiceQuestions.sol: The headquarters of the NHRC is located in New Delhi, though it can also establish offices elsewhere in India with the central government's approval.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the Chairperson or members of the NHRC be re-appointed for a second term under the post-2019 rules?
opts: No, they are completely barred from re-appointment.
Yes, they are eligible for re-appointment.
Only the Chairperson can be re-appointed, not members.
Only members can be re-appointed, not the Chairperson.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 made the Chairperson and members eligible for re-appointment for another term of 3 years.

practiceQuestions.q: Who has the power to remove the NHRC Chairperson or members from office on grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity?
opts: The Supreme Court of India directly
The Prime Minister on Parliamentary resolution
practiceQuestions.sol: The President can remove the Chairperson or members only on the grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity, but only after the Supreme Court, on a reference made to it by the President, has held an inquiry and reported in favor of such removal.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary nature of the recommendations made by the National Human Rights Commission?
opts: Binding on the Central and State Governments
Final judicial decrees equivalent to High Court orders
practiceQuestions.sol: The NHRC's recommendations are purely advisory in nature. It does not have the power to penalize authorities or enforce its decisions, though governments are required to inform the Commission of the action taken within one month.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the NHRC have a limitation regarding investigating human rights violations that occurred more than a year ago?
opts: To prevent administrative backlog and ensure evidentiary viability
Because human rights expire after one year under international law
Due to constitutional restrictions under Article 32
To restrict state governments from interfering in central matters
practiceQuestions.sol: The NHRC cannot inquire into any matter after the expiry of one year from the date on which the act constituting violation is alleged to have been committed, primarily to ensure that evidence is reliable and investigations remain practically manageable.

practiceQuestions.q: What limitation does the NHRC face when inquiring into human rights violations committed by members of the armed forces?
opts: It can directly punish military personnel without consulting the government.
It can only seek a report from the Central Government and make recommendations, rather than investigating suo motu directly through its own investigative machinery in the same manner.
It has absolute jurisdiction over all court-martials and military tribunals.
It is completely prohibited from taking cognizance of any armed forces matters.
practiceQuestions.sol: Regarding armed forces, the NHRC's powers are restricted: it can either seek a report from the Central Government or suo motu/on petition submit recommendations, but it cannot directly exercise its regular penal or comprehensive enforcement powers against military personnel.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the NHRC contribute to human rights jurisprudence even though its orders are non-binding?
opts: By passing legislation directly in Parliament
Through its annual reports submitted to Parliament, intervention in Supreme Court/High Court human rights cases, and public awareness campaigns
By imposing economic sanctions on non-compliant states
By issuing executive orders that supersede state laws
practiceQuestions.sol: The NHRC influences policy and law through its detailed annual reports, interventions in landmark court cases, reviewing constitutional and legal safeguards, and spreading human rights literacy.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are State Human Rights Commissions (SHRCs) established under the Protection of Human Rights Act?
opts: To handle human rights violations concerning subjects enumerated in List II (State List) and List III (Concurrent List) at the state level
To replace the NHRC entirely within respective state territories
To act as judicial branches of the Supreme Court in districts
To manage state police budgets and prison reforms exclusively
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act provides for the creation of SHRCs to decentralize human rights protection and deal specifically with violations related to State and Concurrent List subjects in the respective states.

practiceQuestions.q: What powers regarding civil procedure does the NHRC possess while inquiring into complaints?
opts: Powers of a criminal court with the authority to award prison sentences
Powers of a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
Executive powers equivalent to the Union Cabinet
Legislative powers to amend fundamental rights
practiceQuestions.sol: While inquiring into complaints, the NHRC has all the powers of a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, such as summoning witnesses, receiving evidence on affidavits, and requisitioning public records.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the role of the NHRC in visiting jails and detention centers?
opts: It has no right to visit prisons without prior permission from local courts.
It can visit jails and detention camps to study the living conditions of inmates and make recommendations to authorities.
It can directly order the unconditional release of all undertrial prisoners.
It is mandated to run and manage all state prisons directly.
practiceQuestions.sol: The NHRC is explicitly empowered to visit any jail or any other institution under the control of the State Government, where persons are detained or lodged, to study the living conditions of the inmates and make recommendations thereon.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Protection of Human Rights Act include provisions for the NHRC to promote research in human rights?
opts: To foster human rights culture, spread literacy, and encourage NGOs and academic institutions
To conduct commercial business operations and generate state revenue
To act as a curriculum-setting board for primary schools
To replace university granting commissions across the nation
practiceQuestions.sol: Promoting research and spreading human rights literacy through various media, seminars, and encouragement of non-governmental organizations (NGOs) are key promotional functions mandated to the NHRC under the Act.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Paris Principles relate to the establishment and functioning of the National Human Rights Commission in India?
opts: They are international standards adopted by the UN for national human rights institutions regarding autonomy, pluralism, and independence.
They dictate the economic trade agreements between France and India.
They are European Union human rights directives enforceable in Indian courts.
They provide a military pact for joint intervention in civil wars.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Paris Principles, adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1993, set the international benchmarks for the establishment, composition, independence, and competence of national human rights institutions (NHRIs), guiding institutions like India's NHRC.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the significance of the NHRC's ability to intervene in court proceedings relating to human rights?
opts: It allows the NHRC to act as a prosecutor in criminal murder trials.
With the court's approval, it can intervene in any pending proceeding involving allegations of human rights violations, ensuring institutional advocacy for justice.
It empowers the NHRC to transfer cases from Supreme Court to High Courts.
It lets the NHRC overturn acquittals given by subordinate courts.
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 12(b) of the Protection of Human Rights Act empowers the NHRC to intervene in any proceeding involving any allegation of violation of human rights pending before a court with the approval of such court.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC):
1. It is a constitutional body established under Article 323A of the Constitution of India.
2. The Chairperson of the NHRC must always be a retired Chief Justice of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the NHRC is a statutory body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, not a constitutional body under Article 323A. Statement 2 is incorrect because after the 2019 amendment, the Chairperson can be a retired Chief Justice of India OR a Judge of the Supreme Court, not exclusively a retired CJI.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the NHRC selection committee:
1. The Prime Minister heads the committee as its chairperson.
2. The Chief Justice of India is a member of this selection committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: the Prime Minister is the chairperson of the high-powered selection committee. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Chief Justice of India is NOT a member of the selection committee (though the Speaker of Lok Sabha, Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha, Leaders of Opposition in both houses, and Home Minister are members).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers and functions of the NHRC:
1. It has the power to grant interim relief to victims of human rights violations.
2. It can impose binding penalties and punishments on public servants found guilty of human rights violations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: the NHRC can recommend grant of immediate interim relief to the victims. Statement 2 is incorrect: the NHRC's recommendations are advisory; it cannot directly impose binding penalties, fines, or prison sentences on guilty public servants.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the members of the NHRC:
1. Following the 2019 amendment, the number of full-time members was increased, including women representation.
2. The Chairpersons of the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) and National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) are ex-officio members of the NHRC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: the 2019 amendment increased the number of members (from 2 to 3, including at least one woman) and added the Chairpersons of NCBC and NCPCR as ex-officio members. Wait, let's examine Statement 2 carefully: Yes, the 2019 amendment added the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities and the Chairpersons of NCBC and NCPCR as ex-officio members. Thus both statements are correct? Let's check: Ah, the 2019 amendment actually added NCBC, NCPCR, and Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities as ex-officio members. Therefore, both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct. Let's make sure the option C is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the limitations of the NHRC:
1. It cannot investigate complaints of human rights violations if the incident occurred more than two years ago.
2. It has no jurisdiction to inquire into human rights violations committed in Jammu and Kashmir.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is wrong because the time limit is ONE year, not two years. Statement 2 is wrong because the NHRC's jurisdiction extends across the entire territory of India, including Jammu and Kashmir (especially after the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, which extended the Protection of Human Rights Act to J&K).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the financial autonomy and reporting of the NHRC:
1. The grants to the NHRC are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. The Commission submits its annual report to the Central Government, which then lays it before each House of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: the salaries and allowances of the Chairperson and members are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India, but the administrative grants/expenses are made through budgetary allocations voted by Parliament, not entirely charged on the CFI as a single block grant. Statement 2 is correct: the NHRC submits its annual report to the Central Government, which places it before both Houses of Parliament along with a memorandum of action taken.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding State Human Rights Commissions (SHRCs):
1. An SHRC can inquire into human rights violations in respect of subjects only mentioned in the State List (List II).
2. The Chairperson of an SHRC must be a retired Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because an SHRC can inquire into violations regarding subjects in both the State List (List II) and the Concurrent List (List III). Statement 2 is correct: the Chairperson of an SHRC must be a retired Chief Justice or a Judge of a High Court (amended in 2019 to include a High Court judge as well).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the investigative machinery of the NHRC:
1. The NHRC does not have its own investigative staff and must rely entirely on state police forces.
2. The Commission can utilize the services of any officer or investigation agency of the Central Government or State Government with their concurrence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the NHRC has its own investigative wing headed by an officer not below the rank of a Director General of Police (DGP). Statement 2 is correct: under the Act, the Commission may also utilize the services of any officer or investigating agency of the Central or State Governments with the concurrence of the respective government.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the functions of the NHRC under the Protection of Human Rights Act:
1. It can review the safeguards provided by or under the Constitution or any law for the protection of human rights.
2. It can undertake and promote research in the field of human rights.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Section 12 of the Protection of Human Rights Act outlines these statutory functions, including reviewing constitutional/legal safeguards and promoting research in human rights.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the limitations on the NHRC's mandate during emergencies or external situations:
1. The NHRC has no statutory mandate to study treaties and international instruments on human rights.
2. The Commission is barred from inquiring into any case that is already pending before a state human rights commission or any other statutory judicial commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because studying treaties and international instruments on human rights and making recommendations for their effective implementation is explicitly one of the NHRC's functions under Section 12(f). Statement 2 is correct: the NHRC does not inquire into any matter which is pending before a State Human Rights Commission or any other statutory commission duly inquiring into the same matter, avoiding jurisdictional overlap.
